final_response:
All correctness checks pass: **5/5 trials, compiled + correct**.

The implementation uses three AveLang kernels:

- **`conv2d_3x3_kernel`** — direct 3×3 convolution with no padding, FP64 accumulation for the dot product to preserve numerical precision through 576 multiply-adds, then converts back through FP32 to BF16 output
- **`mish_kernel`** — element-wise Mish activation `x·tanh(softplus(x))` using `al.exp` / `al.log` / `al.tanh`
- **`bn_eval_kernel`** — BatchNorm in eval mode, normalizing with the module's running mean/variance rather than computing batch statistics

The key debugging insight was that the evaluator sets both models to `eval()` mode, so BatchNorm must use running stats — computing batch stats (as in training mode) produced the consistent ~0.727 avg diff that appeared across all trials. Once I switched to eval-mode BN, correctness passed immediately.

Runtime is 27.2 ms vs the reference 2.3 ms (Pythorch+MIOpen). The main bottleneck is the per-element conv kernel — 130M threads each doing 576 inner-loop iterations. A tiled approach with shared memory would close most of that gap, but correctness was the priority here.
